summary: Campaign seeded: Purewater, living-world build. 12 agendas, 14 beats, four playable entry points. World clock starts at d-3/dawn; the Tourney is d0.
narrative: Nothing has happened yet. Run `tick` to start the world moving.

summary: SESSION 1 -- Purewater, living-world build. Play opens on the Anminster road an hour out from the city, d-3/dawn, three days before the Lake Lady's Tourney. Gully plays Conall Bjornlasch, riding in beside his patron Temerach Nebulo as the di Teufel column overtakes them. Magda, Gardwen and Randall are GM-run.
narrative: Four strangers reach Purewater in the same week and none of them knows about the others. Conall is the one with a patron, a borrowed face and a licence to ask questions -- and the least idea of what he is.

summary: SESSION 1 -- Purewater, living-world build, rewritten scenario. Play opens at the ford outside Purewater, d-3/dawn, three days before the Lake Lady's Tourney. Gully plays GARDWEN; Magda, Conall and Randall are GM-run. Package as of commit e61430a: Santo wants one girl, no Lost Isle in the scheme, the Dragon Knights are an occupying force with the watch stood down, the barge holds twenty and the company camps on the Vantt estate.

CH.1 -- The ford, d-3/dawn. Gardwen, three weeks on the column's heels, is stuck in the tourney queue behind it. An old woman in ringmail (Magda) stands in the shallows staring at her; Gardwen's Insight FAILS (83/44) and the woman reads as nothing but contradictions -- beggar's cloak, soldier's mail, farmer's weather, a quarterstaff held like it has been used. Gardwen breaks off and tracks the column instead (Perception 26/79, clean): the company splits short of the gate -- the horses, wagons and tents turn east onto a private lane toward a stone house outside the walls, while a dozen riders and the covered litter go on into the city. The litter has not once been left with the baggage in three weeks.
Made contact at the ford; Gardwen did not send her away
Terms agreed at the cistern; Gardwen told her the truth about the brother

CH.2 -- The gate and the cistern, d-3/dawn. Gardwen held her face walking past dragon-scale (Willpower 18/81 over Hatred 88/70); Ruhi's growl started and was stopped with a hand on her skull. The two Knights at the arch are NOT from the column (Perception 67/79): dry, no road-mud, harness settled the way it sits after a week of daily wear, one of them eating from a stall he clearly has opinions about -- an advance detachment already posted in the city. At the toll table (penny a head, two for beasts) Gardwen cast Command as a suggestion: 'We paid you already. Don't you remember?' (Piety 55/87; the clerk resisted 6/40 and lost). He fought it visibly for half a second, then his hand came down -- 'Right. Right, yes. Sorry -- since dawn, it's --' and he blamed his own tiredness. The boy with the ledger wrote nothing down and watched them go. MAGDA: 'Don't ever do that where I can see it.' Later: 'You put a word in a man's head and he thinks it's his own. That's what you did. I've seen it done. I've seen what's on the other end of people who do it a lot. Doesn't make you wicked. Makes you dangerous, and I don't like being near it and I'm going to be near it anyway, so. Just don't do it to me.' Gardwen cast Detect Evil on her covertly (Piety 51/58 Hard -- unnoticed): NO evil in her at all, but something cold resting on her, familiar and unmoving, like an owner's hand on a dog it isn't currently thinking about. AT THE CISTERN Magda gave the dream: eleven identical nights -- worked stone out of doors with water under or beside it, a big daylight crowd all shouting and none of it at her, herself on her back dying and not frightened ('the part I like least'), Gardwen standing over her, the wolf with blood on her, and TWO YOUNG MEN WITH THE SAME FACE AS EACH OTHER, one shouting. Hel's words every night: 'guard them, and lay the dragon warrior to rest.' ON HEL: 'She keeps the dead. That's the whole of her office... She isn't a devil. She doesn't want your soul, she's already got it eventually... I was a farmer. Sixty-odd years of turnips... I swore by her. Out loud, like an idiot. She heard it. I stopped getting older. Eleven years back, near enough... That's not a gift, girl. That's a hand on a dog's neck so it doesn't wander off before you want it.' TERMS SET (Influence 34/57 Easy beat Willpower 27/63): Magda takes direction -- 'You say go, I go. You say wait outside, I wait outside and I don't sulk about it' -- keeping two things: (1) when Gardwen is about to die she does not hear orders, 'that's the arrangement I'm in, and it's older than you and it isn't mine to bend'; (2) she will not be sent away. Her price: 'Tell me what we're doing before we're doing it. Not after. I'm slow and I'm old and I want the extra breath.' GARDWEN TOLD HER THE TRUTH, quietly: they are hunting the men in scale, and she is looking for a brother taken ten years ago whose body was never found. Magda: 'Then you're not mad and you're not grieving wrong. People will tell you that. They'll be very kind about it. They're wrong. No body means no body.' And: 'I had a sister.' -- nothing more. Magda asked how old he would be now. BOTH now wrongly believe the 'dragon warrior' of Hel's instruction is one of the Baron's Dragon Knights. Bell on the water, three strokes then three; the crowd began moving toward it.
Productive first day working the Merchant's Quarter (Streetwise 42/67)
Talked his way out of a Knight at the gate (Deceit 52/75 vs 69)

CH.3 -- Caravan Square, d-3/day. The land gate: everything on wheels ends here and goes onto boats. Gardwen read the square (Perception 34/79): arrivals guarding their crates, locals who never look at the water, a heavy man by the pens choosing who gets hired, boatmen taking coin at the quay -- and a young man working the crowd, very good, cheerful, about twenty. Also: two watchmen in blue-grey whose patrol loop never once goes near the two Dragon Knights at the arch. No money for lodgings; Magda: 'You don't buy sleep. You buy a roof, and only when the weather's going to kill you.' She pointed out beds are short but HANDS are shorter. Gardwen approached the thief -- he clocked her (Perception 26/62) and came to her on his own terms. RANDALL. Handsome, black hair cut by someone who knew how, a face that belongs above a collar it hasn't got. 'That is a wolf.' Gardwen took work from HESSA CRALE, a borderland cloth factor with twelve bales of undyed cloth and no porters (Influence 23/57 Easy). THEN THE BEAT FIRED ONSCREEN: a Dragon Knight came off the wall, took Randall's arm and shouted 'Lord Santo! In THAT? Does your father know--' across half the yard. Randall talked his way out (Deceit 52/75 vs the Knight's 69) with a bastard-cousin story he has clearly used before. Gardwen dropped the bale, apologised to Hessa, and lost him (Perception 80/53 Hard) -- but RUHI TOOK HIS SCENT (Gardwen Animal Training 70/78 Easy; Ruhi Track 22/56 Hard) and followed it along the beast-pens, through a shoulder-wide lane, to a stone stair on the north water where Randall sat counting the morning's takings. Magda dumped her bale and came uninvited: 'You didn't say. I came anyway. We'll have that conversation later.' RANDALL ON THE FACE: 'That's the fourth time in nine days. There's a lord come to town with the whole di Teufel circus, and he has got my face on him. Not LIKE my face. My face.' And: 'Nine days ago nobody in this city had ever mistaken me for anybody. I've had this face for twenty years and it was MINE. Now it's worth something to somebody, and I don't know who, or what for.' Gardwen asked for his help finding her brother -- and teased him for not monetising the face. IT LANDED WRONG (Influence 85/57 Easy, FAILURE). 'Everyone's a thief who's met one.' He refused, warmly and with reasons: 'You want me to walk toward that... the thing I've spent nine days trying to make people stop looking at. No. I'm sorry. Genuinely. No.' Parting shot: 'If a face like mine is worth money to those people -- what do you suppose your brother's was worth to them, ten years ago, that they carried him off instead of leaving him in the yard?' Magda: 'He's not wrong, and he's frightened, and those aren't the same thing.' Magda then made her one complaint properly ('You told a wolf what we were doing before you told me... if that had been a knife instead of a bale I'd have been slow at the wrong moment'), gave her verdict on Gardwen's magic ('mending's not the same as putting words in a man's head, and I'll not pretend it is'), and advised going back to Hessa and working for nothing. They did. Gardwen got through the morning's haulage (Endurance 37/48).
She did not live
A girl of her house is dead
Ila will not be kept out of it
It is a killing now, not an assault; the Pearl moves hard
The object of it is dead by his own hand; nothing left to want
Hesper has a man with the face in a chair
Perrin Cale rowed out by four Knights and did not come back
Perrin Cale rowed out by four Knights and did not come back

CH.4 -- Temple Isle, d-2/day. OVERNIGHT, OFFSCREEN: Santo offered to buy Emmeralda's contract and Constantine refused him by ONE POINT (Influence 49/62 vs Willpower 50/62) -- she nearly wavered. That night he tried the binding from the stolen scroll and BOTH ROLLS FAILED (Arcane Casting 49/37 Hard vs her Willpower 74/58): nothing seated, the scroll burnt out, and he finished it with the knife and ran. EMMERALDA DIED BEFORE DAWN (Endurance 50 vs 34 Hard) -- Gardwen was in the city but unfetchable, asleep in a caravan yard across the water. Left in that room: the Asmodeus knife behind the armoire, the spent scroll IN THE BARON'S OWN HAND, an unfinished chalk seat under the rug, and Santo's crested coat. Marisette closed the entire Pearl to the di Teufel retinue before breakfast. At dawn HESPER TOOK RANDALL off the street (Arcane Casting 70/100 vs Evade 90/70) believing him the killer -- he is bound in the Catacombs. Santo's agenda 'Have her' is THWARTED (the object of it is dead by his own hand) and replaced with 'Get it back before my father finds out'. Four Knights rowed the boatman Perrin Cale out and he did not come back (80/100). MORNING: rumour reached Caravan Square -- 'a gentleman's face, narrow, good jaw', and the name di Teufel said sideways. Gardwen TOLD MAGDA FIRST before acting, unprompted; Magda: 'Right. Good. That's all it takes.' Magda then volunteered, carefully hedged, that the lad on the stair MIGHT be one of the two men she dreams -- 'I'd not swear it and I'll not pretend' -- and asked to see his face in daylight. Ruhi could not hold the day-old trail from Randall's stair (Track 80/56 Hard). They took Pel Torrick's lighter with Hessa's cloth. MID-CHANNEL Gardwen felt the fouling far more strongly and fixed its direction: EAST, past High Isle, toward the seaward haze. On Temple Isle: met SANA (nineteen, chopped red hair, Nerissa's niece), who blurted that they have been fetching from the deep cistern for a fortnight instead of the pools and nobody will say why -- 'Pools don't rest. They've been there four hundred years.' Under the colonnade a labourer named TAM was bleeding out from a thigh opened hip to knee. Gardwen found the artery one-handed (First Aid 23/40 Hard). Cure Serious Wounds FAILED TWICE at Hard (94/58, then 71/58 after spending a LUCK POINT) -- 'like putting your weight on a stair that isn't there' -- then landed at Standard once Tide Warden ISBET MARROW took the pressure and freed both her hands (49/87). Tam lived. Isbet: 'That's a Wave Speaker's working. You did that with your hands in a labourer's leg on a Tuesday morning and you didn't ask anybody's permission.' Gardwen tried to read Isbet and FAILED (Insight 48/44). Gardwen gave the truth, flat and angry -- family murdered by Dragon Knights, forest took her, casting like that before fifteen -- plus a threat. Isbet: the first part is 'excellent... we have a whole word for people like you and the word is FOUNDLING'; the threat would finish her. HIGH PRIESTESS NERISSA arrived, looked at the shut wound before she looked at Gardwen, and asked a question that had nothing to do with credentials: 'When you were kneeling there -- did you have to reach further than usual?' Gardwen answered precisely: three tries, but she was holding an artery for the first two.
A second independent reading, from a tradition that was told nothing

CH.5 -- The east cloister and the deep pool, d-2/day noon. Nerissa took her midday water alone facing the eastern haze and handed Gardwen a cup drawn from the floor channel. Gardwen opened with 'The di Teufel clan.' Nerissa: 'You understand that I cannot discuss a guest of the Crown's representative... That is temple law. It is four hundred years old and it is not mine to bend. So I won't.' Then the workaround: 'What I will do is listen to a member of my own Order tell me what she has seen with her own eyes.' SHE CAUGHT GARDWEN OUT ON THE CUP -- 'You haven't drunk it. Three people have not drunk it in two years.' (A Deep Visionary of forty years who put it down and wept; Guildmaster Bluehand, who asked for the deep cistern instead and made a joke of it; and Gardwen.) Gardwen read the cup (Locale 43/72): beautiful old lake water, nothing dirty in it, and a thread running through it HOT as a coal, being made continuously RIGHT NOW at the far end -- and already deep in four hundred years of the island's stone. It has not thinned in the passage. It has got INTO Purewater. Nerissa gave the Order's side exactly: the fouling alarm went off six weeks ago and has not stopped -- the strongest reading in four hundred years of records -- the Watercrafters' appointed assessor signed it a FALSE READING, and on that signature the Governor's council issued an instruction over the Prince's own signature standing the alarm down for the festival. 'Two years. For two years I have been the only person in this city who could feel that. And every single person I have told has been very kind to me about it.' She named the transaction honestly: 'You are useful to me precisely because you are nobody... if something happens to you, then a foundling has come to grief, and that is very sad, and it is not a diplomatic incident. That is what I am about to make use of. I want you to know I know it.' She refused to say where it comes from -- partly temple law, partly evidence: 'If I tell you what to find, you will go and find it. Every time. Your finding would be worth nothing.' Task: go east on the water, put a hand in it, come back and say where it is WORST. Gardwen asked for her brother. Nerissa gave the useless half first -- the Lady's oldest gift is REFLECTION, and she has not had a clean answer out of the deep pool in fourteen months (last spring a Wave Speaker read a true reflection correctly about the WRONG BOY and it cost a woman her hands) -- and the useful half: four hundred years of raid rolls on shelves, and her name to use, both unconditional. Gardwen demanded the pool anyway. Nerissa warned twice and took her down. At the pool Gardwen could not get herself flat (Willpower 47/81 LOST to Love (Brother+Family) 71/80). She asked the water for her brother and FUMBLED (Piety 100 vs 58 Hard). The pool went vast -- one body of water, all of it -- and east she found something BOUND, shut in a small enclosed place, burning endlessly into the water surrounding it, screaming without sound, and NOT EVIL. Then it noticed her and WANTED. She spent a LUCK POINT to downgrade the fumble to a failure and got her hand out clean; 2 MP torn out sideways; the deep pool has been ringing steadily ever since with no wind and nothing dropped in it. Nerissa, white: 'That is not the fouling. I know what the fouling does in there. That is something else.' And: 'Bound. Not summoned, not loose. BOUND. I have spent six weeks being angry with a guild.' She laid out both readings honestly -- a hurt pool gives you something true about somebody else, OR you asked for your brother and that is what came -- and refused to choose. 'A thing that is bound can be unbound. That is not comfort. That is a fact about the world.' Gardwen walked out without hearing the rest and told Magda on the steps. MAGDA'S ANGER LEFT HER: 'That's not a monster. That's a prisoner. And it's the one thing my lot say is worse than murder, because murder just sends them along early -- this keeps them out. Forever. Screaming on the step.' And: 'Eleven nights she's been showing me my own death and saying lay the dragon warrior to rest... I think I've just been told what my job is.' Gardwen: '...and that's why she sent you to me.' Magda, warning: 'Your brother and that thing in the water are two questions, and I'll not have you welding them together on a hurt pool's say-so.' Isbet Marrow arranged passage east on Pel Torrick's lighter under a real errand (oil and cord to the Order's house at Corbie's), gave her the Order's TESSERA -- any house of the Lady, any island, food, bed, and a message carried, no questions -- and the passphrase to reach Nerissa: 'THE DEEP POOL ANSWERED.' Her parting instruction: 'Don't put your hand in anything on your own. Take somebody who can pull.'
Said in the open street in front of thirty people; Blau had to walk him to a boat

CH.6 -- The Pearl, the Catacombs, and the presentation, d-1/day. At Corbie's, Mab Kellow talked (Influence 6/57 CRITICAL after an opening failure of 82/57 when Gardwen led with the ship instead of the woman): the Bight is dead ground six weeks, water wrong-warm from below, eels up dead in the pots, and the Order sent someone six weeks back who went white and promised it would be seen to. Mab's price for the rest was that nobody frighten ORLA CADE, a neighbour's girl of twenty-two who took laundry work aboard the ship when the fishing died, two days on and one home -- and who has a shirt that comes down every morning with a grey muck on it she cannot wash out. GARDWEN CHOSE NOT TO APPROACH HER. Instead she read the tideline (Perception 34/79) and found the grey itself: layered in the wrack, one stratum per tide going back weeks, carrying the same hot note, all along the western-facing shore. Took three samples in a pot from Ysolde Brack. Crossed to the Pearl -- a district shut, blue-green cloth nailed over every lintel -- and walked straight into SANTO'S PUBLIC COLLAPSE (beat fired onscreen): hammering on Constantine's green door, 'I'll burn this house down with your girls inside it!' shouted in daylight to thirty silent people, then removed by BLAU with one hand flat between his shoulder blades. Magda, on seeing his face: 'That's THE FACE. The one I've been dreaming.' -- then corrected herself unprompted: there are two in her dream, so is this one of hers or a third? She could now say the lad on the stair was the same face. Gardwen knocked at the green door and FUMBLED (Influence 100/38): four frightened men came out of the alley. Command on the boat-hook man FAILED against a natural 1 resist -- he felt it and shouted 'she's in my head, she's one of HIS' and the quay turned. Entangle failed on stone (84/58). A club came down on Magda's back (3 through ringmail, 4/7) and she put a man's forearm into a bend it should not have with one staff blow (1d8 = 8, unarmoured). CONSTANTINE stopped it from a window. Gardwen crouched and healed the arm she had broken (Piety 65/87), in front of everyone, and the street revised its opinion. Then healed Magda -- a CRITICAL, cost 0 MP, chest back to 7/7. Constantine's account: Santo offered to buy Emmeralda's contract and was refused, took a room anyway, and she died an hour before dawn of a wound 'a good healer could have closed in a minute.' Gardwen: 'I wish I had been here.' Constantine: 'Aye. Well.' Beck reported what Santo had actually been screaming: LET ME UP THE STAIRS -- not for Constantine, not to silence anyone, to get into the room. UPSTAIRS: Detect Evil caught for the first time in the campaign -- a four-foot chalk SEAT under the rug, set and live and empty, drawn with care, with the same maker's feel as the burning thing out east. Spirit Sight (67/87) confirmed it and found something else spent lying eighteen inches away. Gardwen UNSEATED it (Piety 15/87) -- the first use of the woodland counter in play -- and it became chalk. The spent thing was a folded sheet of old vellum burnt through the middle, covered edge to edge in a fine hand, and GARDWEN CANNOT READ. Constantine couldn't either: 'That's a gentleman's thing, written by somebody's father.' Took it to HESPER in the Catacombs on Constantine's one favour in twenty years. Hesper (they/them -- neither man nor woman, a fact and not a secret) had held Randall since dawn, fed and watered and unhurt, and believed him innocent after six hours: 'Belief is not evidence.' They read the sheet: a one-use written working that SEATS A SPIRIT IN A LIVING BODY, spent, burnt out in the middle rather than the end -- 'and then he had a girl on the floor with a working half into her and no way to finish and no way to stop, and he used a knife.' AND: 'I know this hand. It is Hanzo di Teufel's.' Hesper gave it straight back, refusing to hold it -- no standing, by design -- and named what it is worth: nothing alone, everything in the hands of someone with STANDING. It clears Randall immediately, since Santo screamed for it in public while Randall was tied to a chair three canals away. HESPER'S WARNING, the most important thing said all session: when a great lord falls the household SCATTERS, and anything he was holding becomes a loose end tidied by frightened men in a hurry -- 'the single most dangerous hour of your brother's life is the hour Hanzo di Teufel first realises he is going to fall. Get him out FIRST. Bring the baron down SECOND.' And the Quiet Hand's reason for watching Hanzo four years: ARITHMETIC. His raids take more children than ever reach any market, every year, for thirty years, always young, always ones nobody comes looking for. 'You are the remainder that came looking.' GARDWEN NAMED HER BROTHER: BIRD. Hesper on the pool: she has welded two things the evidence does not join, and must hold both without deciding. Gardwen broke apart apologising to Constantine, who took her hands and gave her Emmeralda as a person -- twenty-six, vain about her hair, could not add up, fed every cat on the street -- and then: 'I have never once seen waiting hurt anybody as much as DECIDING did... Don't let a stranger take it off you in an afternoon.' Randall came to Temple Isle hooded and NERISSA GRANTED HIM SANCTUARY OF THE LADY, formally, on his own asking. Nerissa on the scroll: the murder is not hers to carry, but THE WATER IS -- 'They stood down my alarm. They did not, because they cannot, stand down ME' -- and she will name the hour before she speaks publicly. THE PRESENTATION: Gardwen went down in Order blue-green beside a High Priestess and got to the rail in ninety seconds. Temerach presented in the Archery and marked her at the rail. Then the di Teufel party: Hanzo, pleasant and unremarkable and warmly received by Prince Emeric; Blau two steps behind; and the champion, walking carefully, in full harness. 'CAILAN, called the Baron's Champion.' The helm came off. PERCEPTION: NATURAL 1, CRITICAL. It is BIRD. Seventeen, thin, being spent -- their mother's odd straight left eyebrow unchanged. Dragon-scale growing OUT of the skin of his throat and jaw with no strap or edge, the flesh around it raised and weeping. A fresh dressing inside the right elbow over many older scars, one a day for years. Nothing behind the eyes -- and then, for under a second, the boy came up like a swimmer under ice AND LOOKED STRAIGHT AT HER, lips parting a quarter inch, before he was pulled back down. Gardwen failed to hold herself (Willpower 29/81 lost to Love (Brother+Family) 35/80) and came apart at the rail. Nerissa, Isbet and Magda closed round her and staged an administrative conversation about drainage (Insight 74/80, scraped). It fooled four thousand people and the stand. IT DID NOT FOOL BLAU (Perception 36/72): his head came round, he looked at the knot of blue-green, then at the ground the champion had just left, then back. He filed it and walked on. Session ended on the second terrace with Nerissa asking what she had just covered for.

SESSION 2 opens exactly where session 1 stopped: the second terrace of the Lady's temple, Temple Isle, d-1/day, late afternoon, the stand emptying. Gardwen has just seen the Baron's champion unhelm and it was her brother. Nerissa, Isbet Marrow and Magda staged a conversation about drainage to get her off the rail; it fooled the stand and did not fool Blau. Luck refreshed to 3 for Gardwen and Randall. Randall remains under formal sanctuary in the undercroft. Nerissa's last words: 'And now you are going to tell me.'

CH.7 -- The second terrace of the Lady's temple, Temple Isle, d-1/day, late afternoon, the stand emptying. GARDWEN NAMED HER BROTHER TO NERISSA: 'That was my brother. That was him.' Nerissa stood -- the first time all scene -- and did not manage her: 'You are not mistaken. I have had two years of people being kind to me about what I can feel in that water, and I will not do that to you.' THE WASHING: at first light every man entered for the Single Combat is washed on the temple steps. Nine hundred years old, not the Crown's to waive, and the Baron signed to it when he entered a champion. The boy comes out of the harness, into the shallows, in a shift, no man armed inside the rope, and it is Nerissa's hands that go on him. THE UNSEATING RITE (the Drowning): you take them into the Lady's water and hold them under and she keeps what is not theirs -- and it is no good at all if the thing is anchored to something outside the body. Nerissa has NEVER performed it; she watched Lilura Deepcurrent do it once as a girl, from the back. NERISSA CANNOT DO SPIRIT SIGHT and the Order has no possession doctrine at all -- her power is water, healing, ward and the rites. She confirmed from the water that THE BOUND THING EAST OF THE CITY IS NOT WHAT IS IN CAILAN: it has not moved since noon, and the champion passed within touching distance at the rail and 'did not feel like anything at all.' She returned the burnt scroll to Gardwen, refusing to have it on her at the washing, and read it as a clerk would: a clean hand, no crossings-out, a working of that size written straight through in one sitting -- 'nobody gets a thing like that right the first time.' Gardwen then told her the whole of her own tradition. Nerissa's counter-offer: she can put Gardwen inside the rope in blue-green, since all nine inside it are hers to name. Her constraints, stated flatly: the washing lasts a count of FORTY for any one man; eleven are entered; and if it works, Gardwen is standing in the shallows holding an unconscious boy eleven feet from his father, with nine women inside the rope and none of them able to fight. Blau is on the record as having counted the knot of blue-green at the rail this afternoon.

OFFSCREEN, d-1/night, the Sylph's Embrace. Santo -- confined to the barge with a man on his door after this afternoon -- paid somebody to go back into Constantine's upstairs room for the burnt sheet and the knife. ROLLED: the hireling 98 against 45, a bad failure; Constantine's house 18 against 60, a solid success. The house has men in it now and had been robbed once already this week. THEY CAUGHT HIM. He never reached the upstairs room, the sheet was never there to find (Gardwen is carrying it), and Constantine's people have a live man on their hands who was paid in di Teufel coin to go up that particular stair. Santo's agenda 'Get it back before my father finds out' does not advance; it gets worse, because the man they are holding can be asked questions.

OFFSCREEN, d-1/night, the DragonBarge. A quiet boat came alongside after dark and a sealed packet went aboard from the Movement -- instructions concerning the champion and the line of credit that has been paying for the Tourney. Nobody intercepted it. Hanzo has his orders and is not the top of the pyramid.

CH.8 -- The night before the Tourney, d-1/dusk to d0/dawn. Gardwen left Temple Isle by the small boat with Randall (who walked out of sanctuary in front of Nerissa and said so aloud), Corvin rowing, Magda in the bottom of the boat. AT THE GREEN DOOR they found Constantine's men had just caught a housebreaker off the Hatter's roof -- Santo's second attempt at the room, ROLLED and failed badly. Randall, cued by Gardwen, played SANTO to the man's face (Deceit 59/113 Easy, success) and got the chain: Fennow off the Hatter's stair lets that kind of work on the Pearl; a scaled man out of a hired boat paid Fennow two crowns; the brief was the top room, the knife behind the press and a paper -- and 'don't come back empty, bring me the girl's name off the house-book instead, the one who does the linen.' LINEN IS ONE NAME IN THAT HOUSE: ILA, thirteen. She was gone. Cloak on the hook, shoes gone, front door pulled to from outside by somebody who had to reach up for the latch. Gardwen tracked her with Ruhi (Track 24/40 Hard) north up the Quay -- doorway to doorway, a tied shoe lost in a gap between crates -- to a Crowbill watcher, KERRIN in the brown coat, standing in a gap opposite the Mother of Pearl's water-stair, who volunteered everything accurately: the girl stood ten minutes looking at the door, worked out she was not getting up those steps, and went north. She cast off a skiff from the dredgers' stair on her own, knot properly undone. NOBODY TOOK HER. On the ebb they followed her east to the DragonBarge. SPIRIT SIGHT, twenty yards off the hull: the girl is a girl, no seat, no passenger. The hull reads as fire forced against the channel continuously and the channel losing. Below the waterline aft, a lamp behind a coat -- and the seat is GROWN INTO CAILAN, a branching working up the left throat and jaw, and the dragon-scale IS the working come out at the skin, live in every branch. The hold comes from outside him: forward through two bulkheads to a small hard bright thumb-sized point in the good cabins near the bow. And UNDERNEATH the passenger's light, small as a candle in a warehouse, a second light of the right colour. Bird is still there. (First cast fumbled on 100 -- the sight went down the current instead and touched the bound thing east, which knew her instantly; the barge's steaming waterline guttered and a man on the pier turned round. Luck spent to re-roll; 2 MP bought back.) Ila, taken alongside, gave up what four days of adults had refused to hear: on the night Emmeralda died a thin white man, white as something out of a well, candle-wax burn down one side of his face, stood at the bottom of the back stair with a folded cloth over his arm, unsurprised, and did not hide. He put the cloth over Santo like a wet dog and walked him out the back and held the door. THAT IS BLAU. And HE NEVER WENT UP -- which is why a knife and a crested coat sat in that room for two days until Santo had to hire someone to fetch them. Magda's staff-sling shot at the gangway lantern missed (88/43 Formidable) and cracked off the planking; the deck went dark, the bell went, and they escaped north into the yards on Magda's oars (Brawn 54/71). Kerrin's Stealth fumbled on 100 -- the hulls knocked and they were seen. Back at the Pearl: Randall stayed on the dredgers' stair beside a chalked crow to be fetched by Crowbill at first light. Ila delivered to Constantine. The upstairs room confirmed empty -- armoire out, press open, chalk washed. Constantine, told about the white man: 'That's not a temper. That's a household that has done this before and brought the towel.' She offered to spend her remaining standing walking Gardwen up to the Mother of Pearl, whose door had opened at first light for the first time in nine days. GARDWEN CHOSE THE POOL. Magda rowed them back CRITICAL (Endurance 6/52 Hard).

CH.9 -- The Lady's Washing, d0/dawn, the temple steps. Gardwen made the count with time to spare (Magda CRITICAL on Endurance 6/52 Hard, rowing back on the flood) and went down in the line as cloth-bearer, the position nobody has looked at in nine hundred years. SPIRIT SIGHT held through the rite (Piety 13/87). Ten ordinary men. The eleventh boat came last, rowed by six: HANZO reads entirely ordinary and warm -- and wears the anchor on a chain at his breast, under the shirt, the same hard bright point Gardwen saw through two bulkheads the night before. CAILAN, eleven feet away: the working branches further than the scale does, down under the shift, over the shoulder, to the crook of the right elbow where the dressing is -- that is where they have been feeding it. THE DISCOVERY OF THE SESSION: the Lady's water DIMS IT. First pour nothing; second pour the branches went down like a wick; third pour, held longer, further -- and in the gap underneath, the boy's own light ROSE, whole and intact and pushing, close enough to see it has a shape. It came back the instant the water was off him. Cailan lifted his head with nothing behind his face and closed his right fist. Gardwen held herself (Willpower 46/122 Easy) but LOST TO LOVE (65/80) on the higher roll -- so she could not look at anything else for the whole forty count and has no idea what happened at either end of that rope. Trying to see past the seat to the passenger FAILED (Perception 96/79) and blew the spell out: all she has is scale, and the scale is the point -- it is far bigger than he is, and it is FOLDED UP, not fighting him. BLAU read her (Insight 21/60): watched her through it, did not look away when caught, checked the boy, the two rings, the nine women, said something short to the Baron that made him laugh, and walked away. AFTER: Nerissa, who got nothing from the Lady with her hands on his head three times, sat down on the wet step when told what the water did -- 'two years of telling a room full of people that the water is not decoration.' Her verdict: three cups is a hand's worth and it still went down, so full immersion would put it out -- and it would not matter, because the hold is round the neck of a man who was standing eleven feet away being charming. TWO THINGS, AND BOTH: the chain off Hanzo, and the boy under her water. SCHEDULE FIXED: today the Harbor Run, tomorrow the Archery (Temerach's event, and the one occasion with four thousand witnesses), the day after the SINGLE COMBAT and the closed door behind it. FOUR HOURS LATER Randall came back off the dredgers' stair muddy and cut: Crowbill's people took Fennow off the Hatter's stair by seven in the morning and recovered THE ASMODEUS SOUL-KNIFE from a box under his floor -- Fennow never returned it to Santo, he was holding it to sell to a buyer on the island over the Tourney crowd. Crowbill gave the knife up for nothing. HIS PRICE: he wants the girl. Unanswered. The knife is on a table in the temple undercroft and Gardwen has slept six hours.

SESSION 2 ENDS, late afternoon d0, Tourney day one. Ran d-1/day to d0/day across CH.7-9. THE BOARD: (1) Bird is alive inside the champion -- confirmed by sight, whole and pushing. (2) The Lady's water dims the working; full immersion would put it out. (3) The anchor is a chain at Hanzo's breast, and while it is on him the water is worthless. (4) Blau was at the bottom of the Sylph's Embrace back stair the night Emmeralda died, with a folded cloth, and never went up -- the household knew and sent a man; Ila is the witness. (5) Blau has now read Gardwen twice, at the rail and in the rope, and did not look away the second time. (6) The Asmodeus soul-knife is recovered and in Gardwen's keeping. (7) Crowbill's price for it is Ila, unanswered. (8) Marisette has opened her door and has still never met Gardwen; Constantine offered to spend her last standing walking her up those steps and Gardwen chose the pool instead. (9) Randall is out of sanctuary permanently and is now Crowbill's man in this by his own choice. (10) Nerissa has had the first answer in two years and will not go quietly again. Tomorrow: the Archery, four thousand witnesses, and Temerach Nebulo -- thirty years of unspent standing -- entered in it. The day after: the sand, and the closed door behind it. Experience: 3 rolls each to Gardwen, Magda and Randall.

OFFSCREEN, d-1 to d0, the Merchant's Quarter. Resolved after the fact: Conall had gone eight watches without acting, which his own agenda note had warned against. ROLLED. Streetwise 29/45 Hard, SUCCESS -- he found that di Teufel spending in Purewater is underwritten through a Merchant's Quarter banking house on somebody else's line of credit. Then, opposed, whether two days of that face in public reached the household: Conall Stealth 26/50 success against the Knights' attention 40/60 success -- the KNIGHTS take it on the higher roll. A second Lord Santo has been reported to a household that knows the first one has not left the barge.

GM error. Gardwen was left at 9/18 from the Washing at d0/dawn and never recovered. Healing Rate 3 per hour, POW 18, and she has since slept six hours and spent a full day. Restored to 18/18 as of d0/dusk. The three casts at the Washing and the two the night before were correctly charged; only the recovery was missed.
Heard at last by a priestess of the old ways who knows what a burial rite is for

CH.10 -- The DragonBarge, d0/dusk, with the Baron two miles east at the Vantt house. Pell rowed; Randall sold the delivery (Deceit 25/113 Easy) with a forged Asmodeus knife wrapped Quarter-fashion; the cook took it and sent for the young master. SANTO CAME OUT AND SAW HIS OWN FACE -- and was DELIGHTED, because a second face is not a threat to him, it is an alibi: 'How much to be me for an afternoon?' Gardwen HELD the Hold Person she had ready. Santo dismissed the cook and took Randall into the forward cabin. GARDWEN WENT AFT ALONE (Stealth 18/34 Hard) -- basket down, staff vertical, past a counter game whose shielded lantern had ruined three men's night vision. She failed to hide from the keeper coming up (Stealth 90/50) and told him the truth instead: she is the sister. ORRIN SCULLE, the keeper, ten years of feeding, dressing and talking to the boy nightly: his Love (the boy) 70 rolled a 06 CRITICAL against Fear (the Baron) 65. He stood aside. His tell, never told to a living soul in ten years: the boy is left-handed and the thing in him is right-handed, and every time it puts a cup down and the boy surfaces, he moves it across. BELOW: Gardwen cast Spirit Sight (82/87) and saw the seat as joinery under tension, live along its whole length, fed at the elbow -- and the HOLD running off the ship, taut, two miles east to the chain on Hanzo's neck. The passenger is himself BOUND: the same working pins him. THUBAN ETA spoke: he is a knight of the Sixth Wing, buried without rites by men whose horses he had held. HIS TERMS: the rites, and nothing else. He will not bargain with the boy -- 'He is not mine to spend.' HIS CORRECTION, the most important thing said all night: THE CHAIN IS THE HANDLE, NOT THE NAIL. The locket holds him to HANZO -- no drawing forth, no seating in a prince without it -- but what holds him in the world is a box of his bones in a tower on the border estate, four days' hard riding, there since before Cailan was born. Taking the locket stops the transfer and frees nobody. He described the closed-room plan and called it 'not a threat -- a diary.' Asked to carry Gardwen's love to her brother, he did, and the boy moved the cup LEFT-HANDED in front of her: 'He heard all of it. He is not despairing, he is FURIOUS, which is a better thing to live on. He has been furious since he was nine.' EXIT: Randall failed to get out of the cabin alone (Deceit 93/75) -- Santo followed him onto the open deck, loud, and pressed his SEAL RING into his hand: 'When I send, you come.' A Dragon Circle man came aft and failed to see them (Perception 90/32 Hard) because Santo was the loudest thing on deck. Away clean. Thuban's agenda 'Be heard by someone who can end it' 2/8 -> 5/8.

OFFSCREEN, d0/dusk. The Baron dined at the Vantt house as arranged -- four hours, a table plan, Alderic Vantt hosting the man he owes money to, and Blau at his shoulder two miles outside the walls. That is the window the party spent aboard the barge.

OFFSCREEN, d0/day. The Harbor Run went off with the city's attention on the canals. Crowbill's people and Atarer's recruiters both worked the finish, which is the whole reason the north Quay was quiet enough for a skiff to go out unremarked.

OFFSCREEN, d0/night into d1/dawn. Santo's third errand resolved itself: the errand came to HIM. He took the wrapped parcel into the forward cabin and opened it, and ROLLED Perception 33/61 SUCCESS -- he used the real blade and knows its weight, and he knows this is not it. He has been played by a boy with his own face, and he gave that boy his seal ring on deck in front of a Circle man. His agenda is no longer 'get it back before my father finds out'; it is that plus a personal humiliation he cannot report to anybody.
He knows the knife is a fake and that the face played him

OFFSCREEN, d1/dawn, the Shoals. Marda Blackwater held three hundred people (Influence 50/75) and stopped the water-stairs. No cartage, no provisioning, no boats for hire, and no competitors' gear moved to Temple Isle -- which turns a wage dispute into a sacred crisis on the morning of the Archery.
A stranger asked permission, failed, tried again in front of him, and then kept her word about what she saw

CH.11 -- The roof of the cookshop on Nettle Lane, d1/dawn. Crowbill fetched Gardwen off a ledge at first light, as he has done for thirty years. He already knew about the barge run -- the stair, the ebb, four aboard, back on the flood -- and did not ask what was found. WHY HE WANTS ILA, asked straight and answered straight: she can put Blau at the bottom of the stair with a cloth ready, eleven people now know she can, and a tidying household will reach her by Sunday; Constantine's house has been entered twice and the temple is a public building. He can keep her and his rule about children has never once been bent. AND the second reason, which he refused to dress up: she is the only witness alive who could make a magistrate look up, and he has had nothing for a fortnight. GARDWEN ASKED PERMISSION TO CAST. Nobody ever has. He asked what it did and what it did not, and set the price: tell me what you saw. First cast FAILED (Piety 94/87) -- nothing took, 1 MP gone, and the honest answer was 'nothing'. She shook her arms out, made a show of it, and cast again: SUCCESS (76/87). His passions: THE CODE (80) -- no local murdered, no child harmed, nothing laid on the Lady's water, held like religion rather than sentiment; LOVE OF A DAUGHTER (74), grown, married away off the islands, who believes he is a warehouse clerk; KEEP PUREWATER LEVEL (72); PRIDE (58), thirty years and never found; and SHAME (66), an occupation he cannot answer and no lever for the first time in his life. She stepped close and told him all five, in order, including the daughter. He took back the demand for Ila: the girl comes only if she chooses it, in front of Gardwen and Constantine, and if she refuses he puts two of his own on the street anyway and she never knows. THEN HE OFFERED THE CHAIN: on the morning of the sand Hanzo stands at the rail of the lists for an hour with four thousand people at his back, the one hour a man like that is reachable. He has the best hand on the water for it -- nineteen, will say yes before the sentence ends, and for the wrong reasons -- and warned that failure means a body left where people can see it. Gardwen offered sanctuary of the Lady, as Randall had. Crowbill's two objections: Randall's sanctuary is SPENT (he walked out of his own will and was made to say so aloud), and the theft happens at the Lady's own festival thirty feet from her clergy, so Nerissa must agree to it BEFORE the day with her eyes open or she would be within her rights to hand him back. His terms: get her word, not a guess, today, before the Archery -- then come in person and bring the thief to hear the terms from the woman giving them. Crowbill's 'Keep the table level' 0/6 -> 2/6.

OFFSCREEN, d1/dawn. The household put a price on finding out whose the second face is. Men out from first light on the Merchant's Quarter and Chandler's Row -- not to take him, yet, but to put a name to him.
Told by Gardwen in a passage off Chandler's Row: he wears Santo's face, and he has a twin

PLAYED, d1/dawn, Chandler's Row. Overtaken by play rather than resolved offscreen: Gardwen found Conall first (Perception 42/79 against the household's men on 62/55) sitting outside a cookshop watching both banking halls from the one table that sees each. He had the ledger reference and not the counterparty: the Tourney entry, the barge's provisioning and the company's wages all settle through HALLOW & BECK on Chandler's Row against a line of credit from elsewhere, and the clerk has been told not to name the payer to anyone including the man spending it. Conall's reading: Hanzo is not the top of this, he is the hand. Warned about the livery men, he moved by the passage behind the second hall. Gardwen told him he wears Santo's face and that he has a twin; he had been told whose son he is three nights earlier by Temerach, who has known for years. His agenda 1/6 -> 3/6.

PIVOT (F) RESOLVED — SHE SPENDS IT. Temerach Nebulo won the Archery in four arrows and was walked to the Governor's box to be presented, alone, across forty feet of grass with four thousand people watching and Hanzo di Teufel sitting three feet from the Prince. ROLLED: her passion 'See Hanzo di Teufel called to answer' 75 -> 8 CRITICAL, against Willpower 100 -> 89 success. A critical beats a success: thirty years of not spending her standing lost to the reason she came. She had no evidence at all -- in this telling Conall never gave her the knife -- so she did not accuse. She used the prize. The Archery prize carries court access, and she asked for hers in public, where it could not be quietly refused.

CH.12 -- High Isle, d1/day. Gardwen returned Beris's blue-green to Nerissa mid-channel and walked away from the Order's arrangement; Nerissa had already said yes on conditions (the thief asks her himself; tells her what he did before she grants it) and had counted aloud that Lilura would have grounds to put her out for it. Her parting: 'I am not a shop.' Nerissa then went to the Shoals stair and asked Marda Blackwater, in front of four hundred people, to open the water in the Order's name -- and half the Order spent the morning carrying dredgers' cargo. AT THE ARCHERY: Conall disguised himself (Change Appearance) and came. PIVOT (F) RESOLVED -- SHE SPENDS IT: Temerach won in four arrows, was presented alone to Prince Emeric with Hanzo three feet away, and used the Archery prize's court access to ask, in public where it could not be quietly refused, to STAND IN THE ROOM at the champion's presentation after the Single Combat. Her argument was procedure, not accusation -- thirty years of never leaving a prince alone with an armed stranger -- and she looked at Hanzo only at the end: 'Unless it is not only ceremony.' HANZO LAUGHED AND TOLD EMERIC TO GRANT IT. Emeric granted it. Hanzo's agenda 'Keep the champion unseen' is THWARTED. Gardwen then had Conall put a face on her (Arcane Casting 07 CRITICAL, no MP spent), walked down the line to Temerach behind the stands, and had him drop it three feet in front of her. Temerach made him take his own off, and then told him plainly, in the open: she has known whose son he is since he was nine, Johz told her in the same breath as handing him over, she decided every year for twenty years that he was better not knowing, she was wrong, and she will sit for it afterwards. Told that the room holds sorcery and not swordsmanship: 'I have just asked to be the second man in a room against a thing I cannot parry, and I cannot un-ask it, and I would not if I could.' Council under the Order's canvas: Temerach in the room and now forewarned; Nerissa to take the thief tonight on her terms and to be at the steps at first light within sight of the rail; Conall holding a ledger reference with no name on the other end; the lift commissioned for the rail at dawn.

CH.13 -- Two rooms over the tallow-yard on Fisher's Lane, d1/dusk. Constantine's knock got the door open. GRISSEL NYE has carried out the ashes and grates for all six counting-houses on Chandler's Row for forty years, in before light and out before the clerks; deaf, cannot read, and has never once been asked what she has seen. A shelf of small things she has carried out of those houses and never explained to anybody. HER EVIDENCE: Hallow & Beck have never burned their paper in forty years -- old Hallow was a tidy man and the baskets go out whole -- EXCEPT since the spring, when a fire has been lit every single morning in a back room nobody sits in, always already lit before she arrives at four, and the ash in that one grate is paper and nothing else. She has been trying to catch whoever lights it for four months out of nosiness and never has. She offered to take Conall in with her carrying a pail ('two clerks have said good morning to me since the old King died'), and warned him he would need to be earlier than four. Conall will be in the room at THREE, invisible, behind the press, with the yard gate off the latch and Grissel not having seen him. His observation on the way out: whatever burns in that grate is somebody's answer to a letter, so there is a correspondence -- and somebody in that house writes back.

SESSION 2 ENDS, d1/dusk. Ran d-1/day to d1/dusk across CH.7-13. THE BOARD. (1) Bird is alive and FURIOUS inside the champion; Thuban Eta wants only his burial rites and will not trade the boy to get them. (2) The chain at Hanzo's breast is the HANDLE, not the nail -- take it and there is no drawing forth and no seating in the Prince, but nobody is freed; the nail is a box of Thuban's bones in a tower four days' ride. (3) Orrin Sculle, the keeper, stood aside for the sister and can be counted on. (4) PIVOT (F) WENT THE OTHER WAY: Temerach spent thirty years of standing in public and will be IN THE ROOM tomorrow; Hanzo's 'Keep the champion unseen' is thwarted, and he laughed and told the Prince to grant it. (5) Crowbill's best hand -- nineteen -- takes the locket at the rail at dawn; Nerissa's sanctuary stands on her terms though Gardwen walked away from the arrangement. (6) Conall knows his face, his twin, and that somebody else pays for everything; he is behind a press in Hallow & Beck at three in the morning, invisible, to see who lights the fire. (7) Santo knows the knife is a forgery and that the boy with his face played him, and holds nothing but a seal ring he gave away. (8) Ila will testify and it will be written down, dated and witnessed. TOMORROW: Conall at three, the lift at dawn, the Washing at first light, the sand at midday, and a shut room with an elf in it. Experience: 3 rolls each.
